source_quotes: WHY WOULDN'T we trust a stored value if we stored it and or already reviewed it for it to be stored? wouldn't this add computational cost for no reason?
overlap_check: method_22/23/25/40 cover durable-versus-cache parity and write/read path tracing; they do not say to trust stored values or fix the writer. Write/read path tracing is left to method_25 (not repeated here).

payload.name: Stored Values Are Read as Stored
payload.description: A value that was stored after review is trusted when read. A wrong stored value is corrected at its writer and in the stored data, not recomputed on every read.

principles.name: Storing is the commitment
principles.description: If a value was reviewed to be stored, recomputing it at read time costs work and hides the real defect.

heuristics.condition: a reader contains a fallback that recomputes a stored field
heuristics.action: replace the fallback by a fix to the writer

heuristics.condition: a cache holds a field that the durable record lacks
heuristics.action: persist the field or remove the cache

decision_rules.name: Read stored values as they are
decision_rules.condition: code reads a value that a writer stored
decision_rules.outcome: use it unchanged; do not recompute, rescale or second-guess it at read time

decision_rules.name: Fix the writer
decision_rules.condition: a stored value is found wrong
decision_rules.outcome: find the writer that produced it and correct that, then scrub the legacy data that already holds the bad value

decision_rules.name: Scrub with a before-copy
decision_rules.condition: stored data is corrected in bulk
decision_rules.outcome: save a before-copy of what is changed and record what was changed so it can be restored
